classification.difficultyReason: Read a value using the graph scales, calculate rise over run from two points and interpret the gradient as extra years of life expectancy per additional birth year.

content.prompt: The graph shows the life expectancy of people born between 1900 and 2000.

spec.description: Landscape graph with both axis breaks, major solid grid lines, dotted two-unit subdivisions and a black line segment. Display coordinates translate year by 1890 and life expectancy by 30; the broken-axis zero is explicitly labelled.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal labels 1900–2010 every 10 years; vertical principal labels 40–100 every 10 years. The line joins (1900,60) and (2000,85), so L=60+0.25(Y-1900) for 1900≤Y≤2000.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied graph is visible; no reading guides or calculated answers are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: According to the graph, what is the life expectancy of a person born in 1932?

answer.worked: Read vertically from 1932 to the line, then horizontally to the life-expectancy axis: 68 years.

children.label: b
children.prompt: With reference to the value of the gradient, explain the meaning of the gradient in this context.

answer.short: Life expectancy increases by 0.25 years for each additional year in the year of birth.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}m&=\frac{85-60}{2000-1900}\\m&=\frac{25}{100}\\m&=0.25\end{align*}$$
The model predicts an increase of 0.25 years in life expectancy for each additional year in the year of birth.
